newsitem.title: ITALY: Istat chief sees Italy inflation falling slightly.
newsitem.headline: Istat chief sees Italy inflation falling slightly.

text.p: Conditions are right in Italy for continued slight falls in consumer price inflation, the head of national statistics institute ISTAT, Alberto Zuliani, said on Friday.

Answering reporters' questions, he said "the premises exist" to support recent comments by Prime Minister Romano Prodi and Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi that CPI would continue to fall slightly. CPI showed a year-on-year rise of 3.0 percent in October and is expected to drop to 2.6 percent in November.
"We are reading the signals that come from other sectors. Producer prices are falling and so are raw materials prices," Zuliani said. "These are positive signals.
"Wholesale prices are also falling and this, in one way or another, has an effect on consumer prices even though it can take a couple of months to filter through," he said.

Prodi's centre-left government has set an annual average consumer price inflation target of 2.5 percent for 1997 after an average 3.9 percent for this year. ISTAT is due to release official November figures on December 5.
